hook.text: Five thousand years old and still practiced by millions. Ayurveda is India's ancient science of life and balance.

buildup.text: Ayurveda classifies people by three doshas — vata, pitta, kapha — and treats illness by restoring their balance.

discovery.text: Treatment includes diet, herbal medicine, yoga, massage, and purification rituals tailored to each person's body type.

twist.text: Ayurveda treats the person, not the disease. Two patients with the same symptom may get very different treatments.

climax.text: Ayurveda shows that effective medicine doesn't need to look like biomedicine. Holistic systems heal in their own way.

quiz.question: What are the three doshas in Ayurveda?

details.summary: Ayurveda is India's ancient medical system based on balancing three doshas (body constitutions) through diet, herbal remedies, yoga, and lifestyle practices. It remains widely practiced alongside biomedicine in South Asia and has gained global popularity as complementary medicine.
details.whyItMatters: Ayurveda demonstrates a complete medical system with its own anatomy, pathology, and therapeutics that predates and differs from biomedicine. Its persistence challenges the assumption that biomedicine will inevitably replace all other healing.
takeaways: Ayurveda balances three doshas through diet, herbs, and lifestyle
It remains widely practiced in South Asia alongside biomedicine
The system demonstrates complete non-biomedical medical theory

faq.question: What are the three doshas in Ayurveda?
faq.answer: Vata (air and space), Pitta (fire and water), and Kapha (earth and water) are the three doshas. Every person has a unique constitution determined by dosha balance. Disease results from imbalance, and treatment aims to restore each person's natural equilibrium.

faq.question: Is Ayurveda scientifically validated?
faq.answer: Some Ayurvedic practices, particularly certain herbal remedies, have demonstrated clinical efficacy in biomedical trials. The overall philosophical framework of doshas does not map onto biomedical science. Research continues, but results are mixed and quality of studies varies significantly.
